thread.title: Baylor softball prepares for Big 12 quarterfinals against Texas Tech
thread.title_full: Baylor softball prepares for Big 12 quarterfinals against Texas Tech

author: t. j. gough
title: Baylor softball prepares for Big 12 quarterfinals against Texas Tech
text:
Baylor University announced on May 6 that its softball team, seeded eighth, will face No. 2 seed Texas Tech in the quarterfinals of the Big 12 Softball Tournament presented by Allstate. The championship game is scheduled to air on ESPN at 11 a.m. Central Time, with other tournament games available on ESPN+.
The matchup marks Baylor’s fourth consecutive game against Texas Tech and offers the Bears an opportunity to win a game in Bricktown for the third year in a row. Historically, Baylor holds a record of 16-32 in the Big 12 Softball Tournament and is seeking its first victory over Texas Tech in this event since 1997.
Earlier this season, Baylor joined Arizona and Utah as one of only three teams to defeat Texas Tech, coming back from five runs down last Friday in Lubbock. That comeback was their largest since overcoming a seven-run deficit against Kentucky during the College World Series in 2014. The recent win also marked Baylor’s first road victory over a top-five team since defeating No. 5 Texas in May of last year and their first win over a top-two opponent since beating No.1 Oklahoma on February 19, 2023.
Pitching has been key for Baylor this season, with transfers Creager from Georgetown (Arizona State) and Peyton Tanner from Lake Jackson (Tennessee) leading the staff. Creager entered tournament weekend ranked among the conference’s top ten pitchers by innings pitched (113.1), while Tanner also placed among league leaders with at least sixty strikeouts.
Offensively, senior Amber Toven is having her best collegiate season with a .352 batting average and forty-seven runs batted in—the most by any Baylor player since Shaylon Govan’s fifty-four RBIs two years ago. Freshman Kaygen Marshall leads the team with ten home runs—matching Kassidy Krupit’s freshman mark set five years ago—and Gianna Gusman has contributed both as an outfielder and catcher despite injuries elsewhere on the roster.
As they enter postseason play after facing one of their toughest schedules—including twenty-one games against ranked opponents—Baylor looks to build on its resilience shown throughout close contests this year.
